title: The first day of inspection season
body:
Shahbandar, the southwest winds have set in. The western ships are coming down the Strait, and the last China junks are making ready to sail home.

Expected in port: a Javanese rice trader and a pepper ship from the Malabar coast at first light; the Kim Hong, a junk from Guangzhou with porcelain and silk; the Salamat, a Gujarati nau from Cambay with frankincense, seen at the river mouth with a torn foresail; the Arus, a perahu from Perak with tin, mid-morning; and the Kaveri from Pulicat with dyed cotton before noon.

Tides: the 10:15 tide takes both the rice and the pepper ship. The Kim Hong sails at 11:00. The others can wait into the afternoon, but the anchorage holds only three.

Market: the rice stalls are thin. The town wants all twenty-four sacks ashore today. Pepper earns more in dues, and the Chinese buyers will take every bahar of it.

News: a porter says the Kim Hong's factor paid a boatman well last night to keep quiet. It may be nothing. File any customs ruling in the temenggung's name.
notes: The player is a shahbandar; port-wide berthing and inspection authority is a game abstraction; customs rulings are made in the temenggung's name.

Monsoon timing follows docs/research/commodities.md (Pires 1944; Meilink-Roelofsz 1962): western ships arrive on the southwest monsoon (about May to September), Javanese rice on the east winds, China junks sail home on the southwest winds.

Ships, people and incidents are fictional. Tide times are game schedule times, not tidal data. Matches the ships in data/port_day.json and cases case_001 to case_004 without revealing any hidden truth.
